Prealgebra · Lesson 2.2

The Laws of Exponents

Solve this lesson →All lessons

You can always compute 213213 by multiplying thirteen 2s in a row. But for 21002100 that approach is hopeless. Luckily the exponents themselves follow a few simple rules that let you combine powers without ever writing out the factors.

Problem
A strip of paper starts as a single layer. You fold it in half 3 times, creating 2323 layers. Without unfolding, you fold it 4 more times. How many layers does it have now?
Show a hint
  • After 3 folds you have 23=823=8 layers. Each additional fold doubles every existing layer.
Show the full solution
After 3 folds the stack is 23=823=8 layers, and each of the 4 new folds doubles every layer, multiplying the stack by 24=1624=16. 23×24=8×16=12823×24=8×16=128​ Three doublings followed by four more is seven doublings in a row, which is exactly why the exponents add.
Key idea
Product rule. When you multiply two powers with the same base, add the exponents. am×an=am+nam×an=am+n Counting explains it. mm copies of aa followed by nn more copies gives m+nm+n copies altogether.
Problem
Find the missing exponent. 6 ?×68=6156?×68=615
Show a hint
  • The two exponents must add to 15.
Show the full solution
The two exponents on the left have to add to the exponent on the right, so ?+8=15?+8=15 and ?=15−8=7?=15−8=7​. The product rule runs both ways. Forward it merges two powers into one, backward it recovers a missing exponent.

The product rule handles multiplication. Division works the other way. Instead of collecting factors you cancel them, and the exponents get subtracted. The next two problems show why.

Problem
Verify the subtraction pattern by cancelling factors directly. Write 57545457​ as a fraction with every factor of 5 listed in numerator and denominator, then cancel matching pairs. The survivor is a single power of 5. What is its value?
Show a hint
  • List seven 5s on top and four 5s on the bottom, then cancel matching pairs.
Show the full solution
Write out every factor, seven 5s on top and four on the bottom, then cancel. 5754=5⋅5⋅5⋅5⋅5⋅5⋅55⋅5⋅5⋅5=53=1255457​=5⋅5⋅5⋅55⋅5⋅5⋅5⋅5⋅5⋅5​=53=125​ Four cancellations remove four factors from the top and three 5s survive. Subtracting exponents is just counting the survivors.
Key idea
Quotient rule. When you divide two powers with the same base, subtract the exponents. am÷an=am−n(a≠0)am÷an=am−n(a=0) Division cancels equal factors from top and bottom, and subtraction counts what is left.
Problem
Simplify 213×24210210213×24​ to a single power of 2, then give its value.
Show a hint
  • Combine the numerator with the product rule first, then apply the quotient rule.
Show the full solution
Combine the numerator first, then divide. 213×24210=217210=217−10=27=128210213×24​=210217​=217−10=27=128​ Multiplying same-base powers adds the exponents and dividing them subtracts, so the two laws never get in each other's way.

The product and quotient rules both combine two separate powers. A power can also be raised to another power, like (34)5(34)5. That case has a rule of its own, and the next problem works it out.

Problem
Compute (23)4(23)4 by first evaluating 2323, then raising that result to the 4th power. You should arrive at 4096. Write 4096 as a power of 2 and look at the relationship between that final exponent and the original two exponents, 3 and 4.
Show a hint
  • 23=823=8. Now compute 8484.
  • 4096=2124096=212. How does 12 relate to 3 and 4?
Show the full solution
23=823=8, and 84=409684=4096​. Written as a power of 2 that is 4096=2124096=212, and 12=3×412=3×4. The outer exponent asks for four copies of 2323, each copy brings 3 factors of 2, so there are 12 factors in all. Stacked exponents multiply.
Key idea
Power rule. When you raise a power to another power, multiply the exponents. (am)n=am×n(am)n=am×n The outer exponent means nn copies of amam. Each copy has mm factors of aa, so nn copies have m×nm×n factors in all.
Problem
Since 64=2664=26, rewrite 64106410 as a single power of 2. What is the exponent?
Show a hint
  • Substitute 64=2664=26, then apply the power rule.
Show the full solution
Since 64=2664=26, 6410=(26)10=26×10=260,6410=(26)10=26×10=260, so the exponent is 6060​. Rewriting an unfamiliar base as a power of a known base and then multiplying the exponents is the standard move when both numbers are built from the same one.
Problem
A square floor is tiled with square tiles. Each tile has a side length of 4242 centimetres, and the floor has 4343 tiles along each side. Find the area of the floor in square centimetres, expressed as 4n4n. What is nn?
Show a hint
  • The floor's side length in centimetres is 4343 tiles each 4242 cm wide. Find the total side length in cm first.
  • Area equals side length squared. Apply the power rule.
Show the full solution
One side of the floor holds 4343 tiles, each 4242 cm wide. 43×42=43+2=45 cm per side43×42=43+2=45 cm per side The floor is square, so the area is that side length squared. (45)2=45×2=410 sq cm(45)2=45×2=410 sq cm So n=10n=10​. Product rule to build the side, power rule to square it.

The three rules so far all require the same base throughout. But a power can also sit over a product, like (2×5)3(2×5)3. The next problem asks whether the exponent distributes over the multiplication or not.

Problem
Compute (2×5)3(2×5)3 two ways: first as 103103, then as 23×5323×53. Do you get the same answer?
Show a hint
  • 103=1000103=1000. Now find 23×53=8×12523×53=8×125.
Show the full solution
Collapsing the base first, 2×5=102×5=10 and 103=1000103=1000. Distributing the exponent instead, 23×53=8×125=100023×53=8×125=1000. Both routes give 10001000​. Cubing the pair and multiplying the cubes count the same factors, and that is the power-of-a-product rule.
Key idea
Power of a product. An exponent distributes over multiplication. (ab)n=an×bn(ab)n=an×bn This works because (ab)n(ab)n means nn copies of the pair a⋅ba⋅b, and you can regroup to gather all the aa factors together and all the bb factors together.
Problem
Find the positive integer nn such that (9n)4=920(9n)4=920.
Show a hint
  • The power rule gives (9n)4=9n×4(9n)4=9n×4. What must n×4n×4 equal?
Show the full solution
The power rule multiplies the stacked exponents, so (9n)4=9n×4(9n)4=9n×4. For that to equal 920920 the exponents must match, giving n×4=20n×4=20 and n=5n=5​. Backward, the same rule divides. Exponent 20 outside a 4th power means the inner exponent was 20÷420÷4.
Problem
Compute 64÷(24×34)64÷(24×34) without multiplying anything out.
Show a hint
  • Write 6=2×36=2×3 and apply the power-of-a-product rule to 6464.
Show the full solution
Since 6=2×36=2×3, the outer exponent drops onto each factor. 64=(2×3)4=24×3464=(2×3)4=24×34 The numerator is now identical to the denominator, so the quotient is 11​. No multiplying out was needed once 6464 was seen to already contain those factors.

You now have four tools: add exponents when multiplying same-base powers, subtract when dividing, multiply when raising a power to a power, and distribute when a power sits over a product. The last two problems combine all four.

Problem
Simplify (35)4311×35311×35(35)4​ to a single power of 3, then give its value.
Show a hint
  • Apply the power rule to the numerator and the product rule to the denominator. Then divide.
Show the full solution
The numerator is (35)4=35×4=320(35)4=35×4=320 and the denominator is 311×35=316311×35=316. 320316=320−16=34=81316320​=320−16=34=81​ Power rule on top, product rule on the bottom, quotient rule to finish. Deciding which law belongs to which piece before doing any arithmetic is the whole skill.
Problem
Compute 620×415810×320.810×320620×415​. The result is a power of 2. What is the exponent?
Show a hint
  • Write every base as a product of primes: 6=2×36=2×3, 4=224=22, 8=238=23. Apply the power-of-a-product rule to each.
  • After substituting, separate the powers of 2 from the powers of 3.
  • The powers of 3 in the numerator and denominator are equal and cancel completely.
Show the full solution
Rewrite every base in primes. 620=(2×3)20=220×320620=(2×3)20=220×320, 415=(22)15=230415=(22)15=230, and 810=(23)10=230810=(23)10=230. 220×320×230230×320=250×320230×320=250−30=220230×320220×320×230​=230×320250×320​=250−30=220 The exponent is 2020​. The 3s matched top and bottom and cancelled. Break every base into primes first and the laws handle the rest.

Practice these ideas

Practice
A kaleidoscope adds mirrors in two stages. The first tube holds 44 mirrors, and each mirror doubles the number of visible copies of a bead, so the tube shows 2424 copies. You twist on a second tube of 66 more doubling mirrors. Written as a single power of 22, how many copies of the bead do you see through the whole instrument?
Show the solution
Each mirror doubles, so the first tube multiplies by 2424 and the second by 2626. Sending one bead through both means doubling 44 times, then 66 more, which is 1010 doublings all told. Multiplying powers of the same base adds the exponents. 24×26=24+6=21024×26=24+6=210​ That is 10241024 copies, a number you never had to build by hand.
Practice
That 210=1024210=1024 is the reason a kilobyte is not quite 10001000 bytes. Computers count in doublings, and ten doublings overshoot a thousand by just 2424. Engineers shrugged, borrowed the word kilo anyway, and the small fib has stuck ever since.
Practice
A library's main hall holds 3939 books and a small reading room holds 3535 books. The hall holds how many times as many books as the room? Give your answer as a power of 33.
Show the solution
How many times as many is a division. 3935=39−5=343539​=39−5=34​ Dividing powers of the same base subtracts the exponents, so the huge 3939 never has to be written out. The hall holds 8181 times as many books.
Practice
Two identical servers each store 219219 files. Put together, they store how many files in total? Write the total as a single power of 22. Careful, the answer is not 419419.
Show the solution
Two equal stacks add to twice one stack. 219+219=2×219=220219+219=2×219=220​ Doubling lifts the exponent by one and leaves the base alone. It never turns into 44.
Practice
Watch which operation you are in. Multiplying two copies of 219219 adds the exponents and lands far off at 238238. Adding two copies only doubles. When equal powers are added you pull the number of copies out in front, so 219+219=2×219219+219=2×219, and only because that leading 22 matches the base does the exponent climb to 220220.
Practice
A microscope magnifies by 103103 at one setting. To study a single cell you stack that same setting 44 times in a row, each stage feeding its image into the next, for a magnification of (103)4(103)4. Write that as a single power of 1010.
Show the solution
Four stages each multiply by 103103, so the total is 103103 multiplied by itself four times, which is (103)4(103)4. A power of a power multiplies the exponents. (103)4=103×4=1012(103)4=103×4=1012​ A trillion-fold, written without a single zero.
Practice
A square mosaic is 66 tiles wide and 66 tiles tall. An artist refines it so that every tile is rebuilt as a 55-by-55 block of smaller tiles. How many small tiles fill the finished mosaic? Find it by writing the count as (6×5)2(6×5)2 and letting the exponent land on each factor.
Show the solution
Each side once spanned 66 tiles, and every tile is now 55 small tiles across, so a side runs 6×5=306×5=30 small tiles. The mosaic holds (6×5)2(6×5)2 of them, and an exponent on a product drops onto each factor. (6×5)2=62×52=36×25=900(6×5)2=62×52=36×25=900​ Squaring the product and multiplying the squares count the same tiles.
Practice
Three gears feed one counter. Gear A multiplies it by 88, gear B by 44, and gear C by 22. You crank gear A three times, gear B twice, and gear C once. By what single power of 22 has the counter grown?
Show the solution
Rewrite every gear in base 22. Cranking them gives 83×42×2=(23)3×(22)2×21=29×24×21.83×42×2=(23)3×(22)2×21=29×24×21. There is one base now, so add the exponents, 9+4+1=149+4+1=14, giving 214214​. All three gears were powers of 22, so a single base covers them all.
Practice
That is the move worth keeping. When the bases look different but are all powers of one number, rewrite every piece in that one base. The moment a single base rules the expression, the laws take over and the whole thing folds down to one tidy power.
Practice
Two students simplify the same thing and get opposite signs. One writes (−2)4×23(−2)4×23, the other writes −24×23−24×23. Work out each value, then say how far apart the two results sit.
Show the solution
The parentheses decide everything. In (−2)4(−2)4 the sign is inside the power, and four negatives make a positive, so (−2)4=16(−2)4=16. In −24−24 the exponent touches only the 22, and the minus waits outside, so −24=−(16)=−16−24=−(16)=−16. Multiplying each by 23=823=8, 16×8=128,−16×8=−128.16×8=128,−16×8=−128. They sit 128+128=256128+128=256​ apart. The exponent grabs exactly what it touches, no more.
Practice
A puzzle claims that 412412 and 8888 are exactly the same size. Settle it by rewriting each as a power of 22. What single power of 22 do they share?
Show the solution
Send both to base 22. 412=(22)12=224,88=(23)8=224412=(22)12=224,88=(23)8=224 Same base and same exponent, so the puzzle is right and both equal 224224​. Once two numbers share a base, comparing them is just comparing exponents.
Practice
A number is built as 26×5926×59. How many digits does it have once it is written out in full?
Show the solution
A 22 and a 55 make a 1010, but here the 55s outnumber the 22s. The six 22s pair with six 55s, leaving 5353 on its own. 26×59=(26×56)×53=106×125=12500000026×59=(26×56)×53=106×125=125000000 That is 125125 trailing six zeros, so 99​ digits in all.
Practice
Every trailing zero on a whole number is a hidden 1010, and every 1010 is a 22 paired with a 55. That is the whole reason behind round numbers. To learn how many zeros end a giant product, you do not multiply it out, you just count how many 22-and-55 pairs are inside.
Practice
Collapse this tower into a single power of 22. 86×16345×2445×2486×163​
Show the solution
Send every base to 22. On top, 86=(23)6=21886=(23)6=218 and 163=(24)3=212163=(24)3=212, so the numerator is 218×212=230218×212=230. On the bottom, 45=(22)5=21045=(22)5=210 and 2424 stays as it is, so the denominator is 210×24=214210×24=214. Dividing same bases subtracts the exponents. 230214=230−14=216214230​=230−14=216​ That is 6553665536. Once everything sits in one base, the laws flatten the whole tower.
Practice
This sum will not merge, because the powers are not equal. 210+211+212210+211+212 Find its exact value.
Show the solution
Factor out the smallest power, since all three terms contain 210210. 210+211+212=210(1+2+4)=210×7=1024×7=7168210+211+212=210(1+2+4)=210×7=1024×7=7168​ Pulling out the lowest power is the move whenever a sum of powers will not collapse on its own.
Practice
Which is larger, 240240 or 330330? Decide with no calculator by giving both a shared exponent.
Show the solution
Both exponents are multiples of 1010, so give each number the exponent 1010. 240=(24)10=1610,330=(33)10=2710240=(24)10=1610,330=(33)10=2710 The exponents match, so the larger base wins, and since 27>1627>16 the bigger number is 330330​. When the bases will not match, a shared exponent does the same job.
